newsitem.title: USA: OLYMPICS-TOP OFFICIAL APOLOGIZES TO CLEARED OLYMPIC BOMB SUSPECT.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-TOP OFFICIAL APOLOGIZES TO CLEARED OLYMPIC BOMB SUSPECT.

text.p: U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno apologised Thursday to Richard Jewell, the security guard who was an initial suspect in the Olympic bombing a year ago but was later cleared of any involvement.
"I think we owe him an apology. I regret the leak," Reno said at her weekly news conference. She was referring to the way Jewell's name leaked to the news media as a suspect right after the bombing.

Jewell, working as a security guard, discovered a backpack containing the pipe bomb that exploded during the Atlanta Olympics, killing one person and injuring more than 100. A cameraman also died of a heart attack at the scene.
After being hounded for three months by the FBI and the news media, Jewell was publicly exonerated of any suspicion by the Justice Department.
"I regret very much what happened to Mr. Jewell," Reno said. Reno said she would be happy to talk to Jewell but had yet to send him a formal written apology.
Jewell told a congressional committee Wednesday that FBI agents tried publicly to humiliate him when he was a suspect.

"Not only did the FBI accuse the wrong man, its agents in Atlanta and its officials in Washington actively participated in publicly humiliating me and privately violating my constitutional rights," he said.
